label: The Atiyah-Bott Picture
notes: Open by framing the slogan. We are about to do Marsden-Weinstein reduction in infinite dimensions: the space of connections is symplectic, the gauge group acts, and the moment map is curvature. Stress that nothing new is invented; the finite-dimensional machinery of earlier lectures is simply transplanted onto an affine function space over a surface.

label: Principal Bundles and Connections
notes: Recall the bundle data students need. A principal bundle gives vertical directions inside the total space, and a connection is a gauge-invariant choice of horizontal complement, encoded by a Lie-algebra-valued one-form. Emphasize that connections form an affine space, so its tangent vectors are honest horizontal one-forms on the base. That affineness is what later makes everything linear.

label: Curvature of a Connection
notes: Define curvature as the horizontal part of the exterior derivative of the connection form, plus the quadratic bracket term. For an abelian circle bundle the bracket dies and curvature is just the ordinary two-form dA on the surface. Flag flatness as the zero-curvature condition; that vanishing locus is the eventual target of reduction.

label: The Affine Space of Connections
notes: Explain why the space of connections is the right symplectic manifold. Fixing a reference connection identifies the whole space with the vector space of Lie-algebra-valued one-forms. The constant tangent space lets us write one global symplectic form by integrating a wedge product over the surface, paired through the Killing or trace inner product on the algebra.

label: The Atiyah-Bott Symplectic Form
notes: Present the symplectic form explicitly. Pair two connection variations by wedging them and integrating over the closed surface. Skewness comes from the wedge of one-forms; closedness is automatic because the form is constant in affine coordinates; nondegeneracy follows from Poincare duality on the surface. Mention the Fourier diagnostic from the notebook that makes the skew blocks visible.

label: The Gauge Group Acts
notes: Introduce the gauge group as the symmetry. Gauge transformations act on connections by conjugation plus a derivative term; in the abelian circle case a phase function theta shifts A by minus d-theta. Stress two facts: the action preserves the Atiyah-Bott form, and curvature is equivariant. For the circle bundle equivariance degenerates into plain invariance of curvature.

label: Curvature is the Moment Map
notes: This is the heart of the lecture. State that the curvature map sending a connection to its curvature is a moment map for the gauge action. Verify the defining identity: the derivative of the paired moment map equals the symplectic contraction with the infinitesimal gauge vector. Show on the board that this identity is integration by parts, Stokes with no boundary.

label: The Stokes Identity
notes: Slow down on the computation that powers the moment-map property. Choose a gauge element X, a function on the surface, and a variation a. The left side integrates X against the linearized curvature; the right side integrates the gauge vector against a through the form. They agree by moving a derivative across the integral. On a closed surface the boundary term vanishes identically.

label: Flat Connections as the Zero Level
notes: Assemble the reduction. The moment map is curvature, so its zero level set is exactly the flat connections. Quotienting that level by the gauge group is Marsden-Weinstein reduction performed in infinite dimensions. The result is the moduli space of flat connections, a finite-dimensional symplectic space sitting inside an infinite-dimensional construction.

label: Yang-Mills and Representation Varieties
notes: Close with two payoffs. The Yang-Mills functional is the squared norm of the moment map, so its absolute minima are the flat connections at the zero level. And by holonomy the moduli space of flat connections is identified with the representation variety of the surface group into the structure group modulo conjugation. Preview the homework returning to finite dimensions.
